NCAR's adaptive forecast-blending system (DICast), used by Xcel Energy since 2009, cut mean wind forecast error from about 18% to 10.8% by 2014; Xcel estimated US$49m saved (IEEE Spectrum 2015). Forecast error improved, while Xcel's cumulative US$49 million saving remains an attributed estimate. The adaptive weighting description does not establish exactly which learned technique generated the gain. The later US$10 million annual estimate is not an independent verification of the cumulative total. The forecasting system's contribution to savings is Xcel's own estimate relayed by NCAR authors and reporters. The AI character of the system rests on UCAR's reference to artificial-intelligence research and DICast's adaptive bias correction, not on an explicit machine-learning description. So both the AI status and the causal share are unverified.

The trial does not support a specific benefit from the machine-learning decoding, and the therapy as a whole was followed by large pain reductions in both arms.

A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast. The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The OECD Monitor classifies it as an AI system doing event detection and forecasting, and the 2025 Science paper calls it smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

Night-time use for people with suspected nocturnal seizures who could not tolerate EEG, with family or carer consent. Nurse specialists helped install the equipment, and clinicians reviewed selected video and event descriptions. Reports went to the treating professionals, who used them to revise seizure descriptions and care plans.

The system flagged motor events that night staff and carers had not noticed (247 of 707 in Cornwall). In the Danish validation it detected every tonic-clonic seizure in real time. The model's flag reached officers in time to send the car to further (secondary) review before it left the port. Officers physically searched the car, found the 75 kilograms of narcotics and arrested the driver.

The model proposed explanations for experts to assess. It did not authorize a diagnosis or alter treatment on its own.

Already-sequenced unsolved cases, mostly child-parent trios, assembled into a de-identified packet. Each packet held Human Phenotype Ontology terms, any clinician notes, age and sex. It also held a filtered variant table with rarity, predicted effect, ClinVar class and family signal quality. A general-purpose reasoning model asked for the single most plausible molecular explanation and its evidence, not just a ranked gene. The prompt was refined first on cases of known diagnosis. Time elapsed since the original analysis, so that newly published gene-disease links and reclassified variants existed to be found. Expert adjudication under ACMG/AMP criteria by at least two reviewers, CLIA-laboratory confirmation, and return of results by the clinical team.
Clinicians adjudicated candidate explanations, obtained confirmation in a certified laboratory, and returned results to families. A model suggestion alone was not a diagnosis.

O3 Deep Research read each de-identified case packet and proposed the most plausible molecular explanation with its supporting evidence. It diagnosed no one. Humans did the rest. At least two reviewers adjudicated each candidate under ACMG/AMP criteria, a CLIA-certified laboratory confirmed each variant, and the clinical team returned results to families. Its distinct contribution was surfacing candidates in cases that commercial and institutional analyses and multidisciplinary teams had already reviewed. In one early-psychosis case it inferred a 22q11.2 deletion absent from the input data, which genome sequencing then confirmed. Seven of the 18 were rediscoveries already established externally. The study was retrospective, and reviewers were not blinded to model confidence. The authors call for prospective evaluation with comparator baselines, so the gain over renewed human reanalysis is unmeasured.

Dense CCTV coverage (about 500 cameras across five areas) from which a usable frame of the suspect's face could be taken. A police facial recognition database that already held the suspect's photograph from a prior arrest at Kotwali police station.

Investigators used the 32.09 percent match as a lead and confirmed it by arresting and questioning Ali. They then recovered the cash in a raid on Samir's home. In replies dated 25 July 2022, Delhi Police said that it treats matches below 80 percent similarity as false positives that need corroborative evidence.

By DCP (North) Raja Banthia's account, teams took a screengrab of a man seen following the victim. The Israeli software matched it to a prior record from Kotwali police station with a similarity score of 32.09 percent. That gave them Ali's name and his Daryaganj address. A score that low is a lead, not an identification. Police confirmed it by laying a trap and interrogating Ali. The auto-rickshaw trace, the reconnaissance evidence and Samir's arrest came from conventional work. The reports name neither the software nor its vendor.

Researchers selected designs, produced and purified the proteins, assembled target complexes, and checked them through cryo-EM imaging and structure determination.

RFdiffusion generated the backbones of the H3 and TAIL scaffold domains, ProteinMPNN designed their sequences, and AlphaFold2 ranked the candidates. The authors write that the choice of backbone involved a degree of expert-guided selection. People raised the nanobodies, collected and processed the cryo-EM data, and built the models. Three of the four structures used the AI-designed domains. The Galectin10 structure at 2.62 angstroms came from the initial scaffold, iTrimbody, which carries no AI-designed domain, and Protein Data Bank entry 9UBR carries that name. The paper reports one internal comparison. With iTrimbody the Aequorea coerulescens GFP data showed density only for the 5350A trimer. With the AI-designed domains the same protein reached 2.29 angstroms.

An aircraft fitted with Garmin Autoland. Garmin says more than 1,700 are equipped. A rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization that pushed cabin altitude past the system's automatic trigger. A crew that decided to let the automatic sequence run to touchdown rather than take over.

The two pilots, both on oxygen, chose to leave Autoland engaged until touchdown. AvBrief reported that with Autoland engaged the crew could not switch from the guard frequency to the controllers' frequencies.

Autoland engaged itself when cabin altitude exceeded the limit. It declared the emergency to controllers with automated “pilot incapacitation” broadcasts. It flew the descent, approach and landing. The pilots elected to leave it engaged rather than take over. So the landing is the system's work. But the counterfactual, that they could not have landed, is not established. Garmin, the FAA and the operator all call it an automated system. None calls it AI. It is here because the OECD Monitor lists it as an AI system. The Register describes it choosing landing sites from runway length, distance and fuel range.
